teams.name: Arsenal Football Club
teams.ownership_summary: Arsenal is wholly owned by Stan Kroenke through Kroenke Sports & Entertainment (KSE UK Inc), which took the club private in August 2018 after buying Alisher Usmanov's 30% stake and compulsorily purchasing the remaining minority shares. No outside private equity, sovereign or institutional co-investor has been reported.
teams.valuation_source_name: Forbes (The World's Most Valuable Soccer Teams 2026)
teams.notes: Single-owner club with no third-party institutional capital: no PE, sovereign or family-office minority stake has been reported, and no sale process is known as of September 2026. Ownership is via KSE UK Inc, 100% owned by Stan Kroenke; some secondary sources quote 98.89% or 99.7% for interim stages of the 2018 squeeze-out, but the club and Wikipedia describe it as wholly owned. Revenue: club-reported £691.0m for 2024-25 (Deloitte Money League 2026 shows €821.7m, 7th place; Forbes quotes $895m). Valuations diverge by publisher: Forbes 2026 $5.4bn (8th, +59% YoY, after 2025-26 Premier League title), Sportico 2026 $5.43bn (7th), Forbes 2025 $3.4bn, CNBC 2025 8th. The 2018 buyout was funded by a £557m Deutsche Bank loan at KSE level, since replaced by owner loans; the club owed KSE £324.1m per its latest accounts (low-interest, not interest-free). Social totals come from aggregator sites, not the club, and vary by date; the January 2025 per-platform breakdown from Planet Football excludes Facebook (Facebook alone shows ~50.9m). September 2025 saw a board restructuring including the departure of Executive Vice-Chair Tim Lewis.

owners.name: Stan Kroenke / Kroenke Sports & Entertainment (KSE UK Inc)

teams.name: Aston Villa Football Club
teams.ownership_summary: Aston Villa is 100% owned by V Sports (formerly NSWE), the Luxembourg-based holding company of Egyptian billionaire Nassef Sawiris and US billionaire Wes Edens, who bought 55% of the club in July 2018 and the remainder in August 2019. Comcast-backed investment firm Atairos joined V Sports as a minority partner in 2023-24 and holds roughly a third of the holding company; V Sports states it retains full control of all club decisions.
teams.notes: Ownership percentages for Sawiris, Edens and Atairos are stakes in the holding company V Sports, not direct club stakes; V Sports owns 100% of AVFC and states it retains full control. Atairos's stake is reported as ~31.1% (Oct 2024/Nov 2025) and rounded to 32% in Wikipedia's ownership split; the amount Atairos invested was not disclosed in sources found. Revenue: 2024-25 club record of £378m (Deloitte Money League 2026 ranks Villa 14th, €450.2m); 2025-26 accounts not yet found. Valuation: Forbes May 2025 $1.4bn (16th); Forbes and CNBC published 2026 lists on 29 May 2026 (CNBC ranks Villa 21st, revenue $486m, EBITDA -$50m, debt 9% of value) but the 2026 dollar value did not appear in search results, so 2025 is recorded. Sportico put the club 'north of £1bn ($1.27bn)' in 2025 without a precise figure. The women's team sale to the parent company (~£55m) was a PSR-driven intra-group transaction and is disputed as a 'loophole' by critics. Villa Park North Stand redevelopment is under way: capacity drops to ~37,000 for 2026-27 and rises to 50,000+ from 2027-28; 2025 accounts show a £106m facility made available to a subsidiary but undrawn. V Sports also bought 30% of FC Annecy (Ligue 2) in 2026 at a ~€15m valuation as part of its multi-club model (not a club-level deal, excluded from deals).

teams.name: AFC Bournemouth
teams.ownership_summary: 100% owned since December 2022 by Black Knight Football Club (BKFC), a multi-club vehicle whose managing general partner is Bill Foley; NYSE-listed Cannae Holdings is BKFC's largest limited partner (42.4% as of August 2026), alongside a minority group led by Michael B. Jordan, Ryan Sports Ventures and Vegas Golden Knights investors. BKFC also owns FC Lorient (100%) and a majority of Moreirense FC.
teams.notes: Valuations diverge: Sportico's 2025 global list puts Bournemouth at $630m, but Sportico's Premier League ranking page (as surfaced in search) shows $145m, last in the league - the latter looks like an older data point; verify before quoting. Bournemouth is not in Forbes' 2026 top 30. Deloitte Money League 2026 ranks the club 26th with EUR 218.5m revenue for 2024-25 (Sportcal), versus GBP 181.7m turnover in the club's own FY2025 accounts. Cannae's BKFC stake has fallen from 50.1% at the 2022 deal to 44.7% (Dec 2025 10-K) and 42.4% (Aug 2026 Q2 update, $263m invested) as other LPs have come in. Stake percentages for the Michael B. Jordan group and Ryan Sports Ventures are undisclosed. Purchase price of the stadium from Structadene undisclosed. Stadium expansion (c.£85m, Glenigan estimate) has planning consent; funding structure not disclosed. StadiumDB reports owners have put in c.£280m since 2022 via loans (BKFC and Goldman Sachs) and equity; the 2015 Peak6 amount and the 2019 buy-back price were never disclosed.

owners.name: Bill Foley (Managing General Partner, BKFC; club chairman)
Michael B. Jordan (leads minority ownership group)
Ryan Sports Ventures (minority stake in BKFC)
Goldman Sachs (senior secured credit facility, lender)

teams.name: Brentford Football Club
teams.ownership_summary: Matthew Benham, who took full control in 2012, remains majority shareholder through holding company Best Intentions Analytics Limited (BIA), formed in February 2025 to hold his shares in Brentford FC and Spanish club Merida AD. Minority shareholders are Gary Lubner (via This Day Sports and Media Ltd) and Sir Matthew Vaughn (via MARV Bee Ltd) since July 2025, joined in March 2026 by Blackstone executive Prakash Melwani and Universal Music Group CEO Sir Lucian Grainge; stake sizes have not been disclosed by the club.
teams.valuation_source_name: SportsPro (valuation implied by July 2025 minority stake sale)
teams.notes: Stake sizes: the club has never disclosed the minority holdings. Non-authoritative sites (brandsownedby.com, whoistheownerof.com) state Benham 90%, Lubner 5%, Vaughn 5% as of late 2025, before the March 2026 round in which Lubner and Vaughn increased holdings and Melwani and Grainge entered; treat those percentages as unverified. SportsPro reported up to 25% could ultimately change hands. Valuation: the £400m figure is the valuation implied by the July 2025 minority sale (SportsPro; City AM), not a Forbes/Sportico estimate. Sportico's 2026 list references the Brentford LP deal at about $540m and notes LP deals price below control valuations; Brentford does not appear in Forbes' 2026 top 30. Deloitte Football Money League 2026 lists Brentford 30th with EUR 206m revenue for 2024-25 (club accounts state GBP 173.1m turnover, record, with operating loss before player trading of GBP 40.0m and player-trading profit of GBP 27.2m). Debt: GBP 100m Macquarie facility from July 2025 is reported by analysts of the 2024/25 accounts (The Esk, Swiss Ramble), not by a club press release found here. The holding company BIA also owns Spanish club Merida AD. Benham's original takeover was June 2012 (before the 2015 window). Social total is null because no source states a cross-platform total; per-platform counts are as displayed on the pages on 2026-09-28.

owners.name: Matthew Benham (via Best Intentions Analytics Limited)
Gary Lubner (via This Day Sports and Media Limited)
Sir Matthew Vaughn (via MARV Bee Limited)
This Day Sports and Media Limited (Gary Lubner)

teams.name: Brighton & Hove Albion Football Club
teams.ownership_summary: Chairman Tony Bloom has been majority owner since 2009, when he took a 75% stake in return for an interest-free loan to fund the Amex Stadium; he has since funded the club through interest-free shareholder loans (balance £406.5m at June 2025). Deputy chairman and CEO Paul Barber became the second largest shareholder with 1.5% via newly issued shares in August 2025.
teams.valuation_source_name: Forbes (via Wikipedia list of most valuable football clubs)
teams.notes: No private equity, sovereign or institutional capital in the club; funding is Tony Bloom's interest-free shareholder loans (£406.5m owed at June 2025 per 2024-25 accounts; £109.8m had been repaid in 2022-23 and 2023-24 before £107m of new lending). Bloom's 75% stake is the 2009 entry figure; a current precise percentage was not found in an authoritative source (one secondary site cites c.96.4% as of Nov 2025, unverified). Paul Barber holds 1.5% via newly issued shares (Aug 2025), consideration undisclosed. No takeover or stake-sale process reported. Valuation cross-references: Forbes 2025 $910m (rank 27); CNBC 2025 $920m (rank 24) and CNBC 2026 rank 29 with 2024-25 revenue $260m. Deloitte Money League 2026 lists Brighton 21st with EUR 256.8m revenue (2024-25); club accounts state GBP 222.4m for 2024-25, with a £55.8m loss. Bloom also holds stakes in Union Saint-Gilloise, Hearts (29%) and Melbourne Victory (19.1%), relevant to multi-club conversations.

teams.name: Burnley Football Club
teams.ownership_summary: Controlled since December 2020 by Velocity Sports Partners, the sports investment arm of US firm ALK Capital (wholly owned by Alan Pace, Mike Smith and Stuart Hunt), which holds 84% of the club; the remaining 16% sits with individual minority shareholders including JJ and Kealia Watt and Malcolm Jenkins. In November 2025 ALK Capital took upwards of $200m from private equity fund Cynosure | Checketts Sports Capital.
teams.revenue_source_name: The Swiss Ramble (Burnley FC Holdings Limited accounts 2024/25)
teams.notes: Takeover price is disputed: Sportico and Fortune report about £170m; GiveMeSport reports £150m. Valuation left null because no Forbes or Sportico page in the results states a Burnley figure; GiveMeSport's 2025-26 ranking puts Burnley at £200-220m (lowest in the Premier League) citing a blend of Forbes/Sportico/Football Benchmark estimates. Burnley is not in the Deloitte Money League top 20; revenue is from the club's own 2024/25 accounts (Championship season, £71.7m, £28.5m post-tax loss). Accounts show bank borrowings of £105.3m at 7.25-12% secured on Turf Moor and group assets, with £40m reclassified as long-term after a post-year-end renegotiation; theesk.org flags a going-concern note. The Cynosure | Checketts $200m is at the ALK Capital parent level, not a direct club stake, and Bloomberg framed it as a stake sale bringing a new US investor into the Premier League. ALK also bought 99.66% of RCD Espanyol in October 2025 for a reported €130m, so Burnley is now part of a multi-club group. Social total is not stated by any single source, so the per-platform counts are listed separately.

owners.name: Cynosure | Checketts Sports Capital (investment into ALK Capital, the club's parent)
MSD UK Holdings (lender, Michael Dell family office)

teams.name: Chelsea Football Club
teams.ownership_summary: Chelsea is controlled by Clearlake Capital Group, which held 61.5% from the May 2022 takeover of Roman Abramovich's club and in September 2026 bought out co-owners Todd Boehly and Mark Walter (about 12.8% each) for £950m, taking full control at a £5bn valuation including debt. Hansjörg Wyss remains a minority shareholder; the holding company is BlueCo.
teams.notes: Ownership changed on 16 Sep 2026: Clearlake bought out Boehly and Walter (£950m, £5bn valuation incl. debt) after a reported feud; post-deal split reported as Clearlake 86.5% / Wyss 13.5% (some outlets still quote Wyss at 12.83%). Club accounts (year to 30 June 2025) show revenue £490.9m and a Premier League record £262.4m pre-tax loss; Deloitte's €584m for 2024-25 differs by currency and scope. Sportico valued the club at $3.57bn (2025) and $4bn (2026) versus Forbes' $4.2bn (May 2026). The 2024 women's-team sale to sister company BlueCo (£198.7m) is contested for UEFA purposes and its £200m fair value was reported as awaiting Premier League approval. Ares £500m is subordinated PIK debt at HoldCo level, not equity. Social totals vary by source (152.9m vs 146.3m).

teams.name: Crystal Palace Football Club
teams.ownership_summary: Owned by a consortium of individuals: New York Jets owner Woody Johnson (43%, bought John Textor's Eagle Football stake in 2025), Josh Harris and David Blitzer (18% each since 2015) and chairman Steve Parish (just over 10%). In June 2026 the FT reported the owners had appointed Raine Group to explore options including a full sale.
teams.notes: Ownership under review: in June 2026 the FT (via Irish Times / Inside Croydon) reported the owners had appointed Raine Group to run a process that could include a full sale or a controlling stake, alongside stadium-financing options ahead of a second European season. Stake figures vary by source: Wikipedia's 2025-26 season page lists Johnson 45% / Harris 10% / Blitzer 10% / Parish 10%, while wearepalace.uk and the FT-derived reports give Johnson 43%, Harris and Blitzer 18% each (30% combined per FT) and Parish 10% or slightly over; the latter set is used here. Textor's stake is described as 43% or about 45% depending on source. Valuations diverge: Forbes 2025 $790m (ranked 29th); Sportico June 2025 $610m (50th globally); Forbes 2026 keeps Palace at 29th, reported by LondonWorld as around £595m including stadium debt (USD figure not found); the Johnson deal implied £550m. Revenue: club-record £196.6m in 2024-25 (Swiss Ramble; MatchdayFinance rounds to £197m) with operating costs of £239.1m, so the club made a loss. Palace is not in the Deloitte Money League top 20. A 2019 sale memo by Zenith Global Capital Partners marketed 75-90% of the club at a £210m valuation; no deal resulted. Harris and Blitzer invest personally (not via Apollo/Blackstone funds), so no PE fund is recorded as an institutional investor. Selhurst Park capacity is quoted between 25,194 and about 26,000 by different sources; the Main Stand rebuild (started January 2026, Goldman Sachs £125m loan) takes it above 34,000. Social total of 6.7m (givemesport) has no stated as-of date.

teams.name: Everton Football Club
teams.ownership_summary: The Friedkin Group (Texas, chaired by Dan Friedkin, also owner of AS Roma) completed its takeover of Everton on 19 December 2024, buying Farhad Moshiri's majority holding in a deal reported at more than £400m and taking a 98.8% stake after converting shareholder loans into equity. Moshiri, who bought 49.9% in 2016 and built up to 94.1%, exited entirely.
teams.revenue_source_name: Everton FC (2024/25 Annual Report and Accounts)
teams.notes: Stake figures differ by source: ESPN/Sky report The Friedkin Group at 98.8%; The Esk's analysis of filings gives 97.2% after converting the £451m shareholder loan to equity. Takeover price is reported only as 'in excess of £400m'. Valuations: Forbes 2026 $930m (first time on the Forbes list); Sportico $825m (May 2025, via SportsPro commercial guide); CNBC 2026 ranks Everton 27th. Everton is outside the Deloitte Money League 2026 top 20. Revenue £196.7m is club-record turnover for 2024/25 (loss £8.6m); 2025/26 is the first season at the 52,769-capacity Hill Dickinson Stadium (ESPN cited 52,888 at the time of the refinancing). Stadium debt is now the £350m senior secured notes (30-40 year tenor); the prior high-cost Rights and Media Funding, 777/A-Cap and MSP loans have all been repaid. Social total across platforms not stated by any source; Instagram (3M) and TikTok (5.5M) are page counts as seen 2026-09-28.

investors.name: Goldman Sachs (senior secured credit facility, lender)
This Day Sports and Media Limited (Gary Lubner)
Cynosure | Checketts Sports Capital (investment into ALK Capital, the club's parent)
MSD UK Holdings (lender, Michael Dell family office)

deals.headline: Peak6 Investments acquires 25% of AFC Bournemouth
deals.summary: Chicago-based Peak6 Investments bought a 25% stake in AFC Bournemouth from owner Maxim Demin in November 2015; the amount was not disclosed.

deals.headline: Maxim Demin buys back Peak6's 25% stake, retakes full ownership
deals.summary: Peak6 sold its 25% shareholding back to Maxim Demin in January 2019, leaving AFC Bournemouth Limited 100% owned by Demin's AFCB Enterprises Ltd. Terms were not disclosed.

deals.investor: Black Knight Football Club (Bill Foley, Cannae Holdings and limited partners incl. Michael B. Jordan group)
deals.headline: Bill Foley-led Black Knight Football Club buys 100% of AFC Bournemouth for c.£120m
deals.summary: Maxim Demin sold his 100% stake to Black Knight Football Club, whose managing general partner is Bill Foley, with Cannae Holdings taking a 50.1% interest in BKFC (paying $126m) alongside other limited partners, many of them Vegas Golden Knights investors, and a minority group led by Michael B. Jordan. Reported price c.£120m ($147m).

deals.headline: Ryan Sports Ventures takes minority stake in Black Knight Football Club
deals.summary: The Chicago-based Ryan family's sports investment arm, minority owners of the Chicago Bears, acquired an undisclosed minority stake in BKFC, the vehicle that owns AFC Bournemouth.

deals.headline: AFC Bournemouth establishes Goldman Sachs senior secured credit facility
deals.summary: Proceeds of a senior secured credit facility with Goldman Sachs put in place in December 2024 were used to repay £29.4m of City National Bank loans and £6.4m owed to Black Knight Football Club UK Limited, per the club's FY2025 accounts.
deals.source_name: The Esk (analysis of AFC Bournemouth Limited FY2025 accounts)

deals.headline: BKFC buys Vitality Stadium back from Structadene
deals.summary: A newly created BKFC entity, Black Knight Stadium Limited, entered a binding contract to acquire the Vitality Stadium from property company Structadene, which had owned it since 2005 (bought for £3.5m). No price disclosed; the purchase enables the planned expansion to 20,000+ seats.

deals.investor: Black Knight Football Club (owner equity injection)
deals.headline: Owners inject £157.6m of new share capital into AFC Bournemouth in FY2025
deals.summary: AFC Bournemouth Limited's FY2025 accounts show an equity gain of £172.5m, comprising £14.9m profit and £157.6m of share issuance by the owners, alongside the refinancing of owner and bank loans.
deals.source_name: The Esk (analysis of AFC Bournemouth Limited FY2025 accounts)

deals.investor: Black Knight Football Club / AFC Bournemouth
deals.headline: £85m Vitality Stadium expansion to 20,000+ seats clears planning
deals.summary: BCP Council approved the redevelopment of the Vitality Stadium from 11,286 to more than 20,000 seats; Glenigan estimates the project cost at c.£85m. Phase one (corner infills) is due early in 2026/27, the new South Stand upper tier around the start of 2027/28. Funding structure not disclosed.

deals.seller: Alisher Usmanov (Red and White Securities) and minority shareholders
deals.headline: Kroenke buys Usmanov's 30% stake for £550m, takes Arsenal private
deals.summary: KSE, already holding 67%, agreed to buy Red and White Securities' 30.04% stake for over £550m, valuing Arsenal at £1.8bn, and passed the 90% threshold to compulsorily purchase remaining minority shares and de-list the club. Reuters reported the total buyout cost £602m, funded with £45m of Kroenke's own money and a £557m Deutsche Bank loan.

deals.headline: KSE redeems Emirates Stadium bonds, replaces them with owner loan
deals.summary: Arsenal Securities PLC redeemed the two outstanding bonds (about £144m) taken out to build the Emirates Stadium; KSE replaced them with a new owner loan, removing bondholder covenants and the ~£36m debt service reserve requirement. Arsenal Supporters' Trust put KSE's combined refinancing outlay at an estimated £214m.

deals.investor: Bank of England COVID Corporate Financing Facility
deals.headline: Arsenal borrows £120m from Bank of England CCFF
deals.summary: Arsenal confirmed a £120m loan from the COVID Corporate Financing Facility to cover pandemic losses; the club said KSE would assist in repaying it.

deals.headline: Arsenal owes £324.1m in low-interest loans to KSE
deals.summary: Owner loans from KSE, accumulated since 2020-21 and described as low-interest rather than interest-free, stood at £324.1m per the club's accounts.

deals.headline: Sawiris and Edens buy 55% controlling stake in Aston Villa for about £30m
deals.summary: Egyptian billionaire Nassef Sawiris and Fortress co-founder Wes Edens, through NSWE, acquired a 55% stake in Championship club Aston Villa for about £30m ($39m). Previous owner Tony Xia stayed as co-chairman. The club had faced cash-flow problems and a potential HMRC winding-up order over an unpaid £4m tax bill.

deals.headline: Sawiris and Edens buy out Tony Xia's remaining shares to own 100% of Aston Villa
deals.summary: Following promotion to the Premier League, NSWE increased its 55% holding to a full purchase of the club in August 2019, buying out Tony Xia's remaining stake. Terms were not disclosed in the sources found.

deals.seller: V Sports (Nassef Sawiris and Wes Edens)
deals.headline: Atairos takes 20% of V Sports at a valuation above £500m
deals.summary: V Sports, the holding company of Aston Villa, agreed a minority investment from Comcast-backed Atairos valuing V Sports at more than £500m. Atairos obtained a 20% stake in the holding company; V Sports continued to own 100% of AVFC and retain full control of club decisions. The deal was finalised on 12 April 2024.

deals.seller: V Sports (Nassef Sawiris and Wes Edens)
deals.headline: Atairos increases its V Sports stake to about 31%
deals.summary: After its initial 20% entry, Atairos increased its position in V Sports to approximately 31.1% by October 2024, with V Sports subsequently described as owned by Sawiris (34%), Edens (34%) and Atairos (32%). Terms of the increase were not disclosed in the sources found.

deals.headline: Aston Villa sells women's team to parent V Sports at about £55m ahead of PSR deadline
deals.summary: Aston Villa agreed to sell Aston Villa Women to its own parent company V Sports for around £55m on 30 June 2025, with a 90% stake going to V Sports and 10% earmarked for an external US investor. The sale followed concern over a PSR breach after operating losses of around £195m across 2022-23 and 2023-24.

deals.headline: Marc Zahr buys 10% of Aston Villa Women and joins its board
deals.summary: V Sports announced the sale of a 10% stake in Aston Villa Women to Marc Zahr, co-president of Blue Owl Capital, who was to join the women's club's board of directors.

deals.headline: Benham moves Brentford shares into new holding company Best Intentions Analytics
deals.summary: Matthew Benham transferred his shares in Brentford into a newly formed holding company, Best Intentions Analytics Limited (BIA), a restructuring the club says enabled it to secure outside investment.

deals.investor: Gary Lubner (This Day Sports and Media Ltd) and Sir Matthew Vaughn (MARV Bee Ltd)
deals.headline: Lubner and Vaughn take minority stakes in Brentford at c.£400m valuation
deals.summary: Former Belron CEO Gary Lubner and filmmaker Sir Matthew Vaughn became minority shareholders in Best Intentions Analytics, the holding company for Brentford FC. Stake size was not disclosed; reports said up to 25% could ultimately change hands. Benham remains majority shareholder; board appointments subject to Premier League approval.

deals.headline: Brentford agrees £100m facility with Macquarie Bank
deals.summary: £100m interest-bearing facility comprising a £75m four-year term loan and a £25m revolving credit facility, used to repay the club's Barclays overdraft. On relegation the RCF terminates and the term loan is repaid over three years in line with parachute payments.

deals.investor: Prakash Melwani and Sir Lucian Grainge; This Day and MARV increased holdings
deals.headline: Blackstone's Melwani and UMG's Grainge join Brentford as minority investors
deals.summary: Prakash Melwani (Blackstone senior managing director) and Sir Lucian Grainge (Universal Music Group CEO) took minority stakes in Best Intentions Analytics and joined its board; Gary Lubner's and Sir Matthew Vaughn's companies each increased their holdings. Stake sizes and valuation not disclosed. Benham remains majority owner.

deals.headline: Benham stadium-project loans of £22.8m within £104.4m total investment
deals.summary: The club's results for the year to June 2023 state Matthew Benham's total investment in the club stood at £104.4m, including £22.8m of loans relating to the stadium project (Gtech Community Stadium, opened 2020).

deals.headline: CEO Paul Barber acquires newly issued shares, becoming second largest shareholder with 1.5%
deals.summary: Deputy chairman and chief executive Paul Barber bought newly issued shares in the club, taking 1.5% of total shares and becoming the second largest shareholder behind Tony Bloom. Consideration not disclosed.

deals.headline: Tony Bloom lends club £107m in 2024-25, taking owner loans to £406.5m
deals.summary: Per the 2024-25 accounts, owner Tony Bloom loaned the club £107m during the season, taking the interest-free shareholder loan balance to £406.5m after £109.8m had been repaid across the profitable 2022-23 and 2023-24 seasons.

deals.headline: £200m of Bloom's owner loans modified to a convertible note in 2023-24, reinstated as interest-free demand note in 2024-25
deals.summary: £200.0m of the owner loan balance was modified to a convertible note in 2023/24 and then reinstated to an interest-free demand note in 2024/25, per analysis of the club's accounts.

deals.seller: Mike Garlick and other existing shareholders
deals.headline: ALK Capital completes leveraged takeover of Burnley
deals.summary: ALK Capital, led by former Real Salt Lake president Alan Pace, acquired an 84% stake in Burnley from chairman Mike Garlick and fellow shareholders for a reported £170m. The deal was funded with a £65m loan from MSD UK Holdings secured on the club and Turf Moor, plus around £37m drawn from the club's own cash reserves.

deals.headline: MSD UK Holdings lends £65m to fund ALK takeover
deals.summary: Michael Dell's family office MSD UK Holdings provided a £65m loan, reported at 8-9% interest, secured against Turf Moor and the club, with a large portion falling due on relegation. Burnley repaid £32.3m of the loan in 2022 after relegation.

deals.headline: NFL's Malcolm Jenkins becomes minority investor in Burnley
deals.summary: New Orleans Saints safety Malcolm Jenkins' company Malcolm Inc. took a minority stake in Burnley via ALK Capital, becoming the first active NFL player with a stake in a Premier League club. Terms were not disclosed.

deals.headline: JJ and Kealia Watt take minority stake in Burnley
deals.summary: Retired NFL defensive end JJ Watt and NWSL player Kealia Watt acquired a minority ownership stake in Burnley ahead of the club's return to the Premier League. Terms were not disclosed; ALK Capital retains 84% with the remaining 16% held by individual shareholders.

deals.headline: Cynosure | Checketts Sports Capital invests $200m-plus in Burnley parent ALK Capital
deals.summary: Dave Checketts' newly launched private equity fund Cynosure | Checketts Sports Capital Fund I made its first investment, upwards of $200m into ALK Capital, the parent of Burnley and Espanyol. The capital is to fund ALK's football operations across both clubs.

deals.investor: Consortium led by Todd Boehly and Clearlake Capital (with Mark Walter, Hansjörg Wyss)
deals.headline: Boehly-Clearlake consortium completes £4.25bn takeover of Chelsea
deals.summary: A consortium led by Todd Boehly and Clearlake Capital completed the purchase of Chelsea from Roman Abramovich, who was forced to sell after UK sanctions. £2.5bn was paid for the shares with a further £1.75bn committed for investment, giving a headline value of £4.25bn. Clearlake took the majority shareholding while Boehly and Clearlake shared joint control.

deals.headline: Chelsea raises £500m subordinated debt from Ares Management
deals.summary: Ares Management provided £500m of financing structured as a HoldCo payment-in-kind note, intended for stadium and infrastructure investment and the ownership group's multi-club plans rather than transfers.

deals.investor: BlueCo 22 Midco Ltd (Chelsea's parent holding company)
deals.headline: Chelsea sells women's team to sister company BlueCo for £198.7m
deals.summary: Chelsea FC Holdings transferred the women's team to BlueCo 22 Midco, a related company owned by the same ownership group, booking £198.7m from disposal of subsidiaries and a £128.4m pre-tax profit for 2023-24. The transaction helped with Premier League PSR compliance; UEFA does not recognise income from sales to sister companies.

deals.headline: Alexis Ohanian buys 10% of Chelsea Women at £200m valuation
deals.summary: Reddit co-founder Alexis Ohanian acquired a 10% stake in Chelsea FC Women for around £20m, valuing the women's club at £200m, and joined its board.

deals.headline: Clearlake buys out Boehly and Walter for £950m, takes full control of Chelsea
deals.summary: Clearlake Capital, already holding 61.5%, acquired the roughly 12.8% stakes each of Todd Boehly and Mark Walter for a combined £950m, valuing Chelsea at £5bn including debt. Boehly stepped down as chairman; Hansjörg Wyss remains a shareholder.

deals.headline: Harris and Blitzer take 18% each in Crystal Palace with £50m capital injection
deals.summary: Josh Harris (Apollo co-founder) and David Blitzer (Blackstone) each acquired 18% of Crystal Palace, injecting £50m of capital and forming a general partnership with chairman Steve Parish. The investors also committed a further £50m towards stadium development.

deals.headline: John Textor invests £87.5m for 40% of Crystal Palace
deals.summary: US businessman John Textor bought a 40% stake in Crystal Palace for a reported £87.5m (some reports say £86m), joining Parish, Harris and Blitzer as a co-owner. The stake was later held through Eagle Football Holdings.

deals.headline: Eagle Football increases Crystal Palace stake to about 45%
deals.summary: Further investments in spring 2023 and summer 2024 took Textor's Eagle Football holding from about 40% to about 45%. City AM reported a £30m injection to reach around 45%; the amounts per tranche are not stated by the sources found.

deals.headline: Woody Johnson buys Textor's 43% stake in Crystal Palace for about £190m
deals.summary: New York Jets owner Woody Johnson agreed to buy Eagle Football's 43% shareholding for about £190m (about $254m), at a reported club valuation of £550m. The sale removed a UEFA multi-club ownership obstacle to Palace playing in the Europa League; completion was confirmed on 24 July 2025 subject to Premier League and WSL approval.

deals.headline: Crystal Palace secures £125m Goldman Sachs loan for Selhurst Park Main Stand
deals.summary: A £125m loan from Goldman Sachs, tied to the stadium development rather than broadcast income, cleared the way for the Main Stand redevelopment to start in January 2026 with Lendlease as contractor. The project lifts capacity from around 26,000 to more than 34,000; reported cost estimates range from over £150m to £200m.

deals.headline: Farhad Moshiri buys 49.9% of Everton
deals.summary: Moshiri acquired an initial 49.9% shareholding in Everton in February 2016, reported at $270m.

deals.headline: Moshiri raises Everton stake to 68.6%, on course for 77.2%
deals.summary: In September 2018 Moshiri increased his shareholding from 49.9% to 68.6% and said he expected it to reach 77.2% by July 2019.

deals.investor: MSP Sports Capital, Andy Bell, George Downing
deals.headline: MSP Sports Capital-led group lends £158m for Bramley-Moore Dock stadium
deals.summary: At the end of May 2023 MSP Sports Capital, with local businessmen Andy Bell and George Downing, provided a loan that grew to £158m, mostly for stadium construction payments. The loan was repaid by The Friedkin Group during its 2024 takeover negotiations.

deals.headline: 777 Partners agrees to buy Moshiri's 94.1% stake (deal later collapsed)
deals.summary: Miami-based 777 Partners signed an agreement on 15 September 2023 to acquire Moshiri's 94.1% stake, reported at more than £550m, subject to regulatory approval. 777 lent the club over £200m during the process but never completed; the agreement lapsed at the end of May 2024.

deals.headline: 777 Partners takeover collapses after missed deadline
deals.summary: 777 missed the 31 May 2024 deadline to complete, having failed to repay the £158m MSP Sports Capital loan and to satisfy Premier League conditions. Everton began seeking a new buyer.

deals.headline: Friedkin Group agrees to buy Moshiri's majority stake
deals.summary: The Friedkin Group and Farhad Moshiri agreed a deal for Moshiri's majority stake, subject to Premier League, FA, WPLL and FCA approval. The buyer was to assume £150m owed to Rights and Media Funding and about £200m owed to 777 Partners.

deals.headline: Friedkin Group completes Everton takeover with 98.8% stake
deals.summary: Regulatory approvals granted; The Friedkin Group took a 98.8% stake in a deal reported as worth in excess of £400m, making Everton the 10th English top-flight club under majority American ownership.

deals.headline: Friedkin restructures Everton balance sheet with £233.44m share issue and loan-to-equity conversion
deals.summary: Filings showed shares issued for £233.44m to fund working capital and repay Rights and Media Funding and 777/A-Cap loans, with the £451m Moshiri shareholder loan converted into equity.

deals.headline: JPMorgan provides £130m loan to Friedkin Group for Everton and sounds out £300m+ stadium refinancing
deals.summary: Bloomberg reported JPMorgan was lending £130m to The Friedkin Group for the club and approaching institutional investors to raise more than £300m of debt to refinance the stadium.

deals.investor: Consortium of institutional lenders (placement agent JPMorgan Securities)
deals.headline: Everton refinances stadium debt with £350m senior secured notes
deals.summary: A private placement of £350m senior secured notes, co-issued by two club subsidiaries and secured against the new stadium, refinanced Rights and Media Funding borrowings. The club said the offering was oversubscribed multiple times.

deals.headline: Friedkin Group injects further £107m of equity
deals.summary: A further £107m equity injection reported to take total equity put into the club since the December 2024 takeover to nearly £400m.
